newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin backs his government over Iraq crisis.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin backs his government over Iraq crisis.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin, who is vacationing outside Moscow, has backed a statement by his government denouncing U.S. air strikes against Iraq, Itar-Tass news agency said on Thursday.

The government said on Wednesday that U.S. strikes were an "inappropriate" reaction to Baghdad's military operation in its northern region, and demanded that all military actions threatening Iraq's sovereignty be stopped.

"Russian President Boris Yeltsin voiced his agreement with the government's evaluations and proposals concerning the U.S. military actions against Iraq," Tass quoted the presidential press service as saying in a two-paragraph dispatch.
Yeltsin's press office was not immediately available for comment.
Yeltsin has rarely been seen in public since late June, sparking rumours of bad health. Aides insist the 65-year-old is in good shape but needs a rest after his election campaign.
Tass did not make it clear in what form Yeltsin has expressed his endorsement of government policy towards Iraq.
